claim: In Gravesend's church (2026-11-17, round 2 of the church-skyline experiment) buttresses let into the building's outline as notches stood exactly as tall as the eaves and carried the facade's cornice round their tops, so the roofline stepped at every buttress and a blind reviewer read it as a flat crenellated line, a fortress or warehouse. A buttress that stops below the eaves needs its own lower roof sector.
evidence: projects/blood-city/experiments/church-skyline/README.md:46 (round 2 added buttresses) and :124 ('The buttresses step the cornice and read as battlements')
projects/blood-city/experiments/church-skyline/critic-round2.md:10-12: avenue_front, 'the top is a flat crenellated line, so it reads as a fortress or warehouse'
bloodmap/skyline.py:35 and :124 (roof): the low thing, a buttress among them, is a sector whose floor is its top
use: Use a notch for a pilaster that runs to the eaves; for a buttress, make it a raised-floor sector (skyline.roof) lower than the eaves.
